cases.title: POST - Should create comment for existing post
cases.rationale: Creates user, then post, then a comment via /posts/{id}/comments. Asserts 201, Schema.COMMENT (id, post_id, name, email, body), and that post_id, name, email and body match what was sent.

cases.title: POST - Should fail with 422 for invalid email format
cases.rationale: Posts a comment with a malformed email from DataGenerator.generateInvalidEmail(). Asserts 422, Schema.ERROR, and an error for field 'email' whose message contains 'invalid'.
openQuestions: The 'invalid' message wording is copied from the users endpoint and not confirmed for comments. Should the assertion only check that the field is 'email'?
Some malformed formats (e.g. a name with spaces) might be accepted by GoREST validation. That could make the test flaky.

cases.title: POST - Should fail with 422 when body is missing
cases.rationale: Posts a comment with name and email but no body to an existing post. Asserts 422, Schema.ERROR, and an error for field 'body'.

cases.title: POST - Should fail with 422 when post does not exist
cases.rationale: Posts to /comments with post_id 999999999. Asserts 422, Schema.ERROR, and an error for field 'post' whose message contains 'must exist'.
openQuestions: The 'must exist' wording is taken from the posts 'user' error and is not confirmed for comments.

The requirement names /posts/{id}/comments, but this case uses /comments with post_id in the body. A non-existent id in the nested path would likely return 404 instead of 422. Is the body variant the intended one?

cases.title: POST - Should fail with 401 when unauthorized
cases.rationale: Sends a comment POST without the bearer token. Asserts 401 and that the message contains 'authentication'. A non-existent post id is used, so no data is created.
openQuestions: Auth is checked before the post is resolved, so the non-existent post id still yields 401. This follows the posts and users tests, but is not confirmed for the nested comments path.

cases.title: GET - Should list only comments of the given post
cases.rationale: Creates two posts with one comment each. GET /comments?post_id=<first> must return exactly one comment, valid against Schema.COMMENTS, with the matching post_id and id. The second post proves other posts' comments are excluded.
openQuestions: Does ?post_id filtering work reliably on GoREST, given its pagination and caching? The test uses fresh posts, so the expected length of 1 should be deterministic.

cases.title: GET - Should return 404 for non-existent comment
cases.rationale: GET /comments/999999999 must return 404. Asserts the body message equals 'Resource not found'.
